note: Flights got roughly ten times faster and the tab stopped freezing. A beta tester reported ~40-second flights with "page not responding" popups; his file took 46 seconds of frozen tab in Chrome and now takes 4.7. The simulation engine itself produces identical numbers — its 309 golden reference lines are bit-for-bit what 0.070 produced — but three things here DO change results on particular files, and each is called out in the changelog: design files carrying a time step finer than 0.05 s are now flown at 0.05 (a field you can see, override, and read the measured cost of, with a new Guide section explaining why 0.05 is enough); RASAero .CDX1 files whose first simulation has no launch-stage motor now open a configuration that can actually fly; and RockSim staging timers are imported instead of dropped. Also: Auto aero no longer flies every supersonic flight twice, three places the engine recalculated frozen geometry thousands of times per flight are now cached (1.6–3.6x on their own), and a flight that stops early — an unstable rocket tumbling under thrust, no motor igniting — now says so instead of returning a short silent flight.
